question: On what date did the word of the LORD come unto Zechariah, and how are his father and grandfather identified?
opt1: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius; unto Zechariah, the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet
opt2: In the sixth month, in the first year of Cyrus; unto Zechariah, the son of Jehoiada, the son of Benaiah
opt3: In the ninth month, in the fourth year of Artaxerxes; unto Zechariah, the son of Hilkiah, the son of Shaphan
opt4: In the seventh month, in the third year of Darius; unto Zechariah, the son of Asaph, the son of Korah
correct: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius; unto Zechariah, the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet
explanation: Zechariah's prophetic ministry began in the eighth month of Darius's second year (520 BC), identifying him as the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo. Zechariah 1:1 (KJV) - "In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, came the word of the LORD unto Zechariah, the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet, saying,"

question: What fundamental covenant appeal and warning against imitating their fathers does the LORD deliver in Zechariah 1:3-4?
opt1: "Offer unto God thanksgiving, and pay thy vows unto the most High ... for your fathers perished in the wilderness of Zin"
opt2: "Turn ye unto me, saith the LORD of hosts, and I will turn unto you ... Be ye not as your fathers, unto whom the former prophets have cried"
opt3: "Hear, O Israel, the statutes of life, and depart from iniquity ... lest the fury of the LORD consume your vineyards as in the days of old"
opt4: "Sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly, weep between porch and altar ... for your fathers stiffened their necks against Moses"
correct: "Turn ye unto me, saith the LORD of hosts, and I will turn unto you ... Be ye not as your fathers, unto whom the former prophets have cried"
explanation: God calls the post-exilic community to authentic repentance, urging them not to repeat the fatal obstinacy of their pre-exilic ancestors. Zechariah 1:3-4 (KJV) - "Therefore say thou unto them, Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Turn ye unto me, saith the LORD of hosts, and I will turn unto you, saith the LORD of hosts. Be ye not as your fathers, unto whom the former prophets have cried, saying, Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Turn ye now from your evil ways, and from your evil doings: but they did not hear, nor hearken unto me, saith the LORD."

question: What solemn rhetorical question demonstrates the permanence of God's prophetic words over the mortality of human generations in Zechariah 1:5-6?
opt1: "Is my hand shortened at all, that it cannot redeem? or have I no power to deliver your fathers from the pit of corruption?"
opt2: "Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion? yea, your fathers forgot my law in the land of their exile"
opt3: "Your fathers, where are they? and the prophets, do they live for ever? But my words and my statutes ... did they not take hold of your fathers?"
opt4: "Who hath hardened himself against God, and hath prospered? did not your fathers stumble upon the dark mountains of Babylon?"
correct: "Your fathers, where are they? and the prophets, do they live for ever? But my words and my statutes ... did they not take hold of your fathers?"
explanation: Though ancestors and prophets die, God's decreed words and statutes outlive generations and inexorably overtake those who disobey. Zechariah 1:5-6 (KJV) - "Your fathers, where are they? and the prophets, do they live for ever? But my words and my statutes, which I commanded my servants the prophets, did they not take hold of your fathers? and they returned and said, Like as the LORD of hosts thought to do unto us, according to our ways, and according to our doings, so hath he dealt with us."

question: In Zechariah's first night vision, what figure did he behold standing among the myrtle trees in the bottom, and what was behind him?
opt1: An angel clothed in pure linen with a golden measuring rod, standing beside four olive trees and six bronze chariots
opt2: A royal prince of David holding a drawn sword over Jerusalem, surrounded by twelve white stallions with silver bridles
opt3: A high priest wearing a mitre and breastplate of judgment, standing in a vineyard flanked by four winged cherubim
opt4: A man riding upon a red horse among myrtle trees in the glen, and behind him were red, speckled, and white horses
correct: A man riding upon a red horse among myrtle trees in the glen, and behind him were red, speckled, and white horses
explanation: Zechariah sees the Angel of the LORD as a rider on a red horse among myrtle trees, accompanied by angelic equestrian patrols. Zechariah 1:8 (KJV) - "I saw by night, and behold a man riding upon a red horse, and he stood among the myrtle trees that were in the bottom; and behind him were there red horses, speckled, and white."

question: What worldwide reconnaissance report did the angelic horsemen deliver to the Angel of the LORD in Zechariah 1:11?
opt1: "We have walked to and fro through the earth, and, behold, all the earth sitteth still, and is at rest"
opt2: "We have traversed the kingdoms of the north, and behold, the nations prepare war against the sanctuary of Zion"
opt3: "We have surveyed the boundaries of Canaan, and behold, the heathen rejoice over the desolations of Jerusalem"
opt4: "We have searched the four winds of heaven, and behold, the kings of Persia stumble in darkness and confusion"
correct: "We have walked to and fro through the earth, and, behold, all the earth sitteth still, and is at rest"
explanation: The angelic patrol reported that the Persian empire was at peace and rest, while Jerusalem remained desolate. Zechariah 1:11 (KJV) - "And they answered the angel of the LORD that stood among the myrtle trees, and said, We have walked to and fro through the earth, and, behold, all the earth sitteth still, and is at rest."

question: What passionate intercession did the Angel of the LORD utter concerning Jerusalem and the cities of Judah in Zechariah 1:12?
opt1: "O Holy One of Israel, remember thy covenant with Abraham, and restore the glory of the temple before the heathen mock thy name"
opt2: "O LORD of hosts, how long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, against which thou hast had indignation these threescore and ten years?"
opt3: "Arise, O God, plead thine own cause; remember how the foolish man reproacheth thee daily across the seventy years of our affliction"
opt4: "How long, LORD? wilt thou be angry for ever? shall thy jealousy burn like fire against the remnant of the daughter of Zion?"
correct: "O LORD of hosts, how long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, against which thou hast had indignation these threescore and ten years?"
explanation: The Angel of the LORD intercedes over the completion of the 70 years of divine indignation prophesied by Jeremiah. Zechariah 1:12 (KJV) - "Then the angel of the LORD answered and said, O LORD of hosts, how long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, against which thou hast had indignation these threescore and ten years?"

question: Why was the LORD greatly displeased with the prosperous heathen nations that were at ease in Zechariah 1:15?
opt1: Because they offered unclean swine sacrifices upon their altars and refused to acknowledge the God of heaven
opt2: Because they demanded exorbitant taxes in silver from the returned exiles and enslaved the children of Benjamin
opt3: Because God was but a little displeased with Judah, but the heathen nations "helped forward the affliction"
opt4: Because their astrologers mocked the sacred prophecies of Daniel and blasphemed the vessels of the temple
correct: Because God was but a little displeased with Judah, but the heathen nations "helped forward the affliction"
explanation: While God used the nations for measured discipline, they acted with excessive, malicious cruelty to compound Judah's suffering. Zechariah 1:14-15 (KJV) - "So the angel that communed with me said unto me, Cry thou, saying, Thus saith the LORD of hosts; I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy. And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction."

question: What consoling promises regarding Jerusalem's architectural rebuilding and prosperity does the LORD proclaim in Zechariah 1:16-17?
opt1: Twelve gates of pearls shall be erected, walls of jasper built, kings of Persia shall bring gold, and Jerusalem shall rule all nations
opt2: The Ark of the Covenant shall be found in the caves of Nebo, the priests shall wear golden vestments, and peace shall flow like a river
opt3: The glory of Solomon shall be doubled, foreign armies shall be drowned in the Kidron valley, and David's throne established forever
opt4: God is returned to Jerusalem with mercies, His house shall be built, a line stretched upon Jerusalem, cities spread abroad through prosperity, and Zion comforted and chosen
correct: God is returned to Jerusalem with mercies, His house shall be built, a line stretched upon Jerusalem, cities spread abroad through prosperity, and Zion comforted and chosen
explanation: God promises mercy, the measuring line for construction, prosperity in her cities, and divine comfort for chosen Zion. Zechariah 1:16-17 (KJV) - "Therefore thus saith the LORD; I am returned to Jerusalem with mercies: my house shall be built in it, saith the LORD of hosts, and a line shall be stretched forth upon Jerusalem. Cry yet, saying, Thus saith the LORD of hosts; My cities through prosperity shall yet be spread abroad; and the LORD shall yet comfort Zion, and shall yet choose Jerusalem."

question: In Zechariah's second night vision, what did the four horns represent according to the interpreting angel in verse 19?
opt1: "These are the horns which have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem"
opt2: "These are the four kingdoms of brass, iron, silver, and gold seen by Daniel"
opt3: "These are the four corners of the altar of burnt offering which sanctify the sacrifices"
opt4: "These are the four winds of heaven which execute vengeance upon the kings of the north"
correct: "These are the horns which have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem"
explanation: The four horns represent the oppressive Gentile powers from all four compass directions that scattered God's covenant people. Zechariah 1:18-19 (KJV) - "Then lifted I up mine eyes, and saw, and behold four horns. And I said unto the angel that talked with me, What be these? And he answered me, These are the horns which have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem."

question: What craftsmen did the LORD reveal next, and what specific divine mission were they appointed to execute in Zechariah 1:21?
opt1: Four masons who came to quarry living stones from Mount Moriah to lay the cornerstones of the sanctuary
opt2: Four carpenters (craftsmen) who came to fray the horns and cast out the horns of the Gentiles that scattered Judah
opt3: Four goldsmiths who came to fashion golden crowns for Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest
opt4: Four iron-smiths who came to forge chains to bind the princes of Babylon and the kings of Persia
correct: Four carpenters (craftsmen) who came to fray the horns and cast out the horns of the Gentiles that scattered Judah
explanation: God raises four carpenters/craftsmen to terrify ('fray') and smash down the oppressive Gentile horns. Zechariah 1:20-21 (KJV) - "And the LORD shewed me four carpenters. Then said I, What come these to do? And he spake, saying, These are the horns which have scattered Judah, so that no man did lift up his head: but these are come to fray them, to cast out the horns of the Gentiles, which lifted up their horn over the land of Judah to scatter it."

question: In Zechariah's third night vision, what did the man with a measuring line in his hand state as his objective?
opt1: "To measure the foundation of the temple, to determine the thickness of the inner sanctuary wall"
opt2: "To mark out the borders of the twelve tribes of Israel, from Dan even unto Beersheba"
opt3: "To measure Jerusalem, to see what is the breadth thereof, and what is the length thereof"
opt4: "To divide the valley of Hinnom for the burials of the heathen who fought against Zion"
correct: "To measure Jerusalem, to see what is the breadth thereof, and what is the length thereof"
explanation: Zechariah sees a surveyor going forth to measure the dimensions of Jerusalem. Zechariah 2:1-2 (KJV) - "I lifted up mine eyes again, and looked, and behold a man with a measuring line in his hand. Then said I, Whither goest thou? And he said unto me, To measure Jerusalem, to see what is the breadth thereof, and what is the length thereof."

question: Why was the young surveyor told that Jerusalem would inhabit as towns without walls, and what would the LORD be unto her?
opt1: Because King Darius decreed that no stone fortifications should be built, yet the LORD would blind all enemy archers
opt2: Because an earthquake would level all earthly ramparts, yet the LORD would overshadow the city with a pillar of cloud and fire
opt3: Because peace would reign across all continents, and the angels of heaven would stand as living battlements around Judah
opt4: Because of the multitude of men and cattle therein, and the LORD "will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and will be the glory in the midst of her"
correct: Because of the multitude of men and cattle therein, and the LORD "will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and will be the glory in the midst of her"
explanation: Jerusalem's explosive population would overflow stone walls, protected by God Himself as a wall of fire and inner glory. Zechariah 2:4-5 (KJV) - "And said unto him, Run, speak to this young man, saying, Jerusalem shall be inhabited as towns without walls for the multitude of men and cattle therein: For I, saith the LORD, will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and will be the glory in the midst of her."

question: What urgent summons to escape is delivered to the Jewish exiles remaining in Mesopotamia in Zechariah 2:6-7?
opt1: "Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north ... Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon"
opt2: "Arise, depart, for this is not your rest ... cross the Euphrates before the king of Persia closes the mountain passes"
opt3: "Blow the horn in the streets of Susa ... gather your children and your silver, and journey toward the holy mountain"
opt4: "Rend your garments in the cities of the Medes ... flee as sheep from the wolves, and return unto the land of your fathers"
correct: "Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north ... Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon"
explanation: God warns remaining exiles to flee Babylon ('the land of the north') before judgment falls upon her. Zechariah 2:6-7 (KJV) - "Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the LORD: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the LORD. Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon."

question: With what tender and protective anatomical metaphor does the LORD describe anyone who dares to harm His covenant people in Zechariah 2:8?
opt1: "For whosoever woundeth you pierceth the heart of the Almighty"
opt2: "For he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye"
opt3: "For he that afflicteth you crusheth the signet ring upon my right hand"
opt4: "For whosoever despoileth you reacheth into the holy of holies of my sanctuary"
correct: "For he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye"
explanation: God views touching His people as touching the most sensitive and precious part of the body—the pupil (apple) of His eye. Zechariah 2:8 (KJV) - "For thus saith the LORD of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye."

question: What dramatic reversal of fortunes will occur when the LORD shakes His hand over the oppressive nations in Zechariah 2:9?
opt1: "Their golden chariots shall be burned in smoke, and their princes shall pay double tribute to the priests of Levi"
opt2: "They shall wander blind in the desert of Paran, and their storehouses shall be opened to feed the poor of Jerusalem"
opt3: "They shall be a spoil to their servants: and ye shall know that the LORD of hosts hath sent me"
opt4: "Their kings shall walk barefoot in chains of brass, and their daughters shall be handmaids to the daughters of Zion"
correct: "They shall be a spoil to their servants: and ye shall know that the LORD of hosts hath sent me"
explanation: In poetic justice, the imperial masters will become plunder ('a spoil') to their former subjects and slaves. Zechariah 2:9 (KJV) - "For, behold, I will shake mine hand upon them, and they shall be a spoil to their servants: and ye shall know that the LORD of hosts hath sent me."

question: What ecstatic reason for singing and rejoicing is proclaimed to daughter Zion in Zechariah 2:10?
opt1: "Shout aloud, O daughter of Jerusalem: for thy walls are rebuilt and the golden vessels are restored to the sanctuary"
opt2: "Blow the trumpet, O daughter of Zion: for the kingdom of David is established and all thine enemies are put to shame"
opt3: "Sing praises with stringed instruments: for the seventy weeks of Daniel are accomplished and thy King reigneth in glory"
opt4: "Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion: for, lo, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith the LORD"
correct: "Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion: for, lo, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith the LORD"
explanation: Zion is called to exultant song because the LORD Himself is coming to take up residence in her midst. Zechariah 2:10 (KJV) - "Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion: for, lo, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith the LORD."

question: What Gentile expansion into covenant fellowship is foretold to occur 'in that day' in Zechariah 2:11?
opt1: "Many nations shall be joined to the LORD in that day, and shall be my people: and I will dwell in the midst of thee"
opt2: "All the kings of the Gentiles shall bring their crowns to Jerusalem, and shall be tributary unto the governor of Judah"
opt3: "The islands of the sea shall cast their idols into the deep, and shall send seventy bullocks annually to the temple"
opt4: "The seed of Ishmael and the princes of Egypt shall learn the language of Canaan, and shall serve as watchmen upon Zion's walls"
correct: "Many nations shall be joined to the LORD in that day, and shall be my people: and I will dwell in the midst of thee"
explanation: Many Gentile nations will be grafted into God's covenant people, sharing in His personal indwelling. Zechariah 2:11 (KJV) - "And many nations shall be joined to the LORD in that day, and shall be my people: and I will dwell in the midst of thee, and thou shalt know that the LORD of hosts hath sent me unto thee."

question: What unique, first-time biblical title is given to the territory of Judah in Zechariah 2:12?
opt1: "The mountain of peace", which the Lord of hosts shall establish above all continents forever
opt2: "The holy land", which the LORD shall inherit as His portion, and shall choose Jerusalem again
opt3: "The city of truth", which shall never be plucked up nor thrown down from generation to generation
opt4: "The garden of God", wherein living waters shall flow eastward and westward unto the great sea
correct: "The holy land", which the LORD shall inherit as His portion, and shall choose Jerusalem again
explanation: This is the only verse in the entire Old Testament where the phrase 'the holy land' specifically occurs. Zechariah 2:12 (KJV) - "And the LORD shall inherit Judah his portion in the holy land, and shall choose Jerusalem again."

question: With what universal command of cosmic silence and divine awakening does Chapter 2 conclude in verse 13?
opt1: "Keep silence before him, all the earth: for the King of glory hath entered into his sanctuary"
opt2: "Tremble, ye islands and kings: for the Lord GOD cometh with ten thousands of his saints to judge"
opt3: "Be silent, O all flesh, before the LORD: for he is raised up out of his holy habitation"
opt4: "Bow down, every knee under heaven: for the Lord of hosts hath made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all nations"
correct: "Be silent, O all flesh, before the LORD: for he is raised up out of his holy habitation"
explanation: All humanity is commanded to stand in reverent silence as God rouses Himself from His heavenly dwelling to act. Zechariah 2:13 (KJV) - "Be silent, O all flesh, before the LORD: for he is raised up out of his holy habitation."

question: Across Zechariah Chapter 2, what primary theological truth unifies the vision of the measuring line, the wall of fire, and the call to flee Babylon?
opt1: The strategic necessity of constructing high stone ramparts and deep moats before the armies of Greece advance
opt2: The permanent exclusion of all Gentile nations from entering the courts of the sanctuary or learning the Torah
opt3: The re-establishment of the political monarchy of David under a temporal king to conquer the Persian satrapies
opt4: God's passionate protection, boundless future expansion, and personal indwelling presence among His restored covenant people
correct: God's passionate protection, boundless future expansion, and personal indwelling presence among His restored covenant people
explanation: Chapter 2 centers on divine security without physical walls, God Himself as fire and glory, and the inclusion of many nations. Zechariah 2:5 (KJV) - "For I, saith the LORD, will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and will be the glory in the midst of her."

question: In Zechariah's fourth night vision, who is seen standing before the Angel of the LORD, and who stands at his right hand to resist him?
opt1: Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, and Satan standing at his right hand to resist him
opt2: Zerubbabel the governor standing before the Lord of hosts, and Sanballat the Horonite standing to accuse him
opt3: Zechariah the prophet standing before the altar, and an angel of death standing to challenge his vision
opt4: Ezra the scribe standing before the cherubim, and the prince of Persia standing to hinder his petition
correct: Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, and Satan standing at his right hand to resist him
explanation: Zechariah beholds a courtroom scene where Joshua the High Priest represents Israel, facing Satan's adversarial accusations. Zechariah 3:1 (KJV) - "And he shewed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, and Satan standing at his right hand to resist him."

question: With what divine rebuke does the LORD silence Satan's accusation, and what metaphor describes Joshua's miraculous deliverance?
opt1: "Depart from me, thou accuser of the brethren; for Jerusalem is sealed with blood: is not this an olive branch in the rock?"
opt2: "The LORD rebuke thee, O Satan; even the LORD that hath chosen Jerusalem rebuke thee: is not this a brand plucked out of the fire?"
opt3: "The Lord of hosts shall tread thee under foot, O adversary: is not this high priest a consecrated vessel of pure gold?"
opt4: "Hold thy peace, O wicked one; for my covenant with Levi standeth sure: is not this a cedar planted by the rivers of water?"
correct: "The LORD rebuke thee, O Satan; even the LORD that hath chosen Jerusalem rebuke thee: is not this a brand plucked out of the fire?"
explanation: God rebukes Satan on the basis of His sovereign election of Jerusalem, describing Joshua as a half-burned stick rescued from the fire. Zechariah 3:2 (KJV) - "And the LORD said unto Satan, The LORD rebuke thee, O Satan; even the LORD that hath chosen Jerusalem rebuke thee: is not this a brand plucked out of the fire?"

question: What symbolic attire did Joshua wear before the Angel, and what command was given to those who stood before Him?
opt1: Joshua was wearing sackcloth and ashes; and the Angel commanded that he be washed in running water and anointed with myrrh
opt2: Joshua was clothed in linen stained with blood; and the Angel commanded that seventy rams be offered to cleanse his vestments
opt3: Joshua was clothed with filthy garments; and the Angel commanded: "Take away the filthy garments from him ... I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee, and I will clothe thee with change of raiment"
opt4: Joshua was wearing chains of iron; and the Angel commanded that the fetters be broken and a purple robe placed upon him
correct: Joshua was clothed with filthy garments; and the Angel commanded: "Take away the filthy garments from him ... I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee, and I will clothe thee with change of raiment"
explanation: The filthy garments symbolize defiling sin and guilt, which are sovereignly removed and replaced with festive robes of righteousness. Zechariah 3:3-4 (KJV) - "Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and stood before the angel. And he answered and spoke unto those that stood before him, saying, Take away the filthy garments from him. And unto him he said, Behold, I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee, and I will clothe thee with change of raiment."

question: What headpiece did Zechariah urge to be set upon Joshua, symbolizing the restoration of high priestly holiness and dignity?
opt1: A golden royal diadem inscribed with the twelve tribes of Israel, set upon his head by two cherubim
opt2: A crown of polished silver with a blue ribbon, placed upon his forehead by Zerubbabel the governor
opt3: A linen turban anointed with the oil of consecration, tied upon his head by the interpreting angel
opt4: "Let them set a fair mitre upon his head. So they set a fair mitre upon his head, and clothed him with garments"
correct: "Let them set a fair mitre upon his head. So they set a fair mitre upon his head, and clothed him with garments"
explanation: The prophet interjects, requesting the clean priestly headdress ('fair mitre') bearing the plate 'HOLINESS TO THE LORD'. Zechariah 3:5 (KJV) - "And I said, Let them set a fair mitre upon his head. So they set a fair mitre upon his head, and clothed him with garments. And the angel of the LORD stood by."

question: What conditional covenant promises and heavenly access did the Angel of the LORD protest unto Joshua in verse 7?
opt1: If he walks in God's ways and keeps His charge, he shall judge God's house, keep His courts, and receive "places to walk among these that stand by"
opt2: If he offers daily sacrifices without blemish, his sons shall reign as kings in Jerusalem and conquer all the satraps of Darius
opt3: If he cleanses the sanctuary from idols, an angel of light will stand at his right hand and grant him visions of the throne room
opt4: If he fasts on every new moon, the storehouses of heaven will open and grain will multiply fourfold in the valleys of Judah
correct: If he walks in God's ways and keeps His charge, he shall judge God's house, keep His courts, and receive "places to walk among these that stand by"
explanation: Faithful stewardship gives Joshua judicial authority over the temple and direct spiritual access ('places to walk') among angelic beings. Zechariah 3:6-7 (KJV) - "And the angel of the LORD protested unto Joshua, saying, Thus saith the LORD of hosts; If thou wilt walk in my ways, and if thou wilt keep my charge, then thou shalt also judge my house, and shalt also keep my courts, and I will give thee places to walk among these that stand by."

question: How are Joshua and his priestly fellows described, and what premier Messianic title does the LORD introduce in Zechariah 3:8?
opt1: They are "pillars of the sanctuary"; for the LORD declares: "Behold, I will raise up the Lion of the tribe of Judah"
opt2: They are "men wondered at" (signs/tokens); for the LORD declares: "Behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH"
opt3: They are "watchmen of the dawn"; for the LORD declares: "Behold, I will establish the Prince of Peace upon Mount Zion"
opt4: They are "messengers of the covenant"; for the LORD declares: "Behold, I will send forth the Sun of righteousness with healing"
correct: They are "men wondered at" (signs/tokens); for the LORD declares: "Behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH"
explanation: Joshua and his priests were sign-men pointing forward to the ultimate Priest-King, God's Servant 'the BRANCH'. Zechariah 3:8 (KJV) - "Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou, and thy fellows that sit before thee: for they are men wondered at: for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH."

question: What mysterious stone is laid before Joshua, how many eyes are upon it, and what singular atonement promise is engraved upon it?
opt1: A jasper stone with twelve facets; God will inscribe the names of the apostles, and cleanse the temple in forty days
opt2: An altar stone with four horns; God will pour out holy oil upon it, and forgive the sins of the princes in a single hour
opt3: A stone with seven eyes; God will engrave the graving thereof, and "I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day"
opt4: A foundation stone with seven golden crowns; God will seal it with His signet, and turn away the captivity of Israel forever
correct: A stone with seven eyes; God will engrave the graving thereof, and "I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day"
explanation: The stone possesses seven eyes (complete divine omniscience) with the promise of removing the land's iniquity in a single day (the cross). Zechariah 3:9 (KJV) - "For behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua; upon one stone shall be seven eyes: behold, I will engrave the graving thereof, saith the LORD of hosts, and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day."

question: With what classic portrait of Messianic fellowship and peaceful domestic neighborliness does Chapter 3 conclude in verse 10?
opt1: "In that day shall all the families of the earth feast together upon the holy mountain with songs of everlasting joy"
opt2: "In that day shall the wolf and the lamb feed together, and none shall hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain"
opt3: "In that day shall every household offer thanksgiving with unblemished calves, and peace shall abide in all their borders"
opt4: "In that day, saith the LORD of hosts, shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree"
correct: "In that day, saith the LORD of hosts, shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree"
explanation: Comprehensive atonement results in shared shalom, where neighbors hospitably invite one another under vine and fig tree. Zechariah 3:10 (KJV) - "In that day, saith the LORD of hosts, shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree."

question: What is the primary theological theme demonstrated through Joshua's cleansing in Zechariah Chapter 3?
opt1: Divine justification and priestly restoration by grace alone through the imputed righteousness of the coming Messiah
opt2: The permanent legal superiority of the Aaronic sacrificial system over all future covenants
opt3: The necessity of human ascetism and forty-day ritual washings to achieve ceremonial perfection
opt4: The political supremacy of the high priest over the civil governor in governing post-exilic Judah
correct: Divine justification and priestly restoration by grace alone through the imputed righteousness of the coming Messiah
explanation: Chapter 3 illustrates justification: the adversary silenced, dirty rags replaced with clean robes by God's grace through the Branch. explanation: The inscription once reserved exclusively for the High Priest's golden plate ('HOLINESS UNTO THE LORD') now marks common horse bells and cooking pots, with commercial corruption banished forever. Zechariah 14:20-21 (KJV) - "In that day shall there be upon the bells of the horses, HOLINESS UNTO THE LORD; and the pots in the LORD's house shall be like the bowls before the altar. Yea, every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holiness unto the LORD of hosts: and all they that sacrifice shall come and take of them, and seethe therein: and in that day there shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of the LORD of hosts."
